data.title: Insulin signalling to mTOR mediated by the Akt/PKB substrate PRAS40
data.authors: Vander Haar E; Kim DH et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Insulin signals to mTORC1 through Akt phosphorylation of the inhibitor PRAS40.
data.abstract_excerpt: Insulin stimulates protein synthesis and cell growth by activation of the protein kinases Akt (also known as protein kinase B, PKB) and mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR). It was reported that Akt activates mTOR by phosphorylation and inhibition of tuberous sclerosis complex 2 (TSC2). However, in recent studies the physiological requirement of Akt phosphorylation of TSC2 for mTOR activation has been questioned. Here, we identify PRAS40 (proline-rich Akt/PKB substrate 40 kDa) as a novel mTOR binding partner that mediates Akt signals to mTOR.

extracted_findings.effect: Insulin signals to mTOR via Akt phosphorylation of PRAS40, relieving its inhibition of mTORC1
